correctness.rationale: All six single-insertion profile-change vectors are computed directly and pairwise distinct. Their exact occurrence conditions are separately proved, including both boundary choices, internal pairs, constant and length-one cases. The no-00 avoidance count F_(n+2), matching-endpoint count trace(M^(n-1))=L_(n-1), and inclusion–exclusion give all four closed formulas for every n>=2. An exact direct insertion program checks every word for n<=16; an independently constructed transfer/deletion checker confirms endpoint trace and saturation implication. Computational checks are corroborative, not the all-length proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The more general sequence-profile framework allows arbitrary word lengths and other read lengths, but its enumerated global code/profile results do not provide a uniform fixed-source insertion-ball theorem. Likewise, global string reconstruction from multispectra does not by itself count local insertion image sizes; potential dominating unindexed channel-ball enumeration remains the historical risk.

originality.rationale: The closest primary DNA-profile articles count global profile spaces and construct codes, while the exact inspected 2026 published result counts all binary adjacent-pair multispectra and singleton reconstruction classes, not fixed-source one-insertion profile output sets. Jacquet–Knessl–Szpankowski count global/cyclic Markov types, not insertion neighborhoods. Direct comparison of the mathematical objects shows none of these claims implies the insertion-specific pointwise law, four all-length class counts, or the deletion-to-insertion saturation implication. The independent raw-insertion proof is not a reindexing of the one-deletion law. Unindexed prior equivalent calculations remain possible.

value.rationale: The distribution of distinct observable dinucleotide profiles under a single insertion is a natural local channel-ambiguity invariant, distinct from the n+2 possible inserted words and from the total profile count in the whole word space. The result completely classifies every binary source word, all four ambiguity strata and their limiting probabilities, gives the first six-profile saturation length, and proves an edit-channel comparison with deletion. These features address reconstruction under synchronization edits without claiming an unproved coding gain.
